title: Two loads
topic: A friend is timing two loads of laundry before heading out
blurb: A friend is trying to wash and dry two loads before leaving the house.
prompt: A friend just texted this in the group chat. If one line doesn't add up, tap it.

segments.label: The deadline
segments.text: I have to leave in two hours, and I've still got two loads that need to be washed and dried.

segments.label: The machines
segments.text: The washer takes 30 minutes a load, and the dryer next to it takes 45.

segments.label: The sigh
segments.text: That's 75 minutes start to finish for one load, so two loads is two and a half hours. I'm not going to make it.

segments.label: The fallback
segments.text: If anyone's nearby later, I may need to borrow a shirt.

conclusion: 75 minutes a load times two is two and a half hours, so I won't be done before I leave.

flaws.original: I can wash the second load while the first one dries: 30 plus 45 plus 45 is two hours. I can just make it.
flaws.corrupted: That's 75 minutes start to finish for one load, so two loads is two and a half hours. I'm not going to make it.

diagnosis_choices.label: You can wash the second load while the first one dries: 30 + 45 + 45 is two hours. You'd finish on time.
The dryer is the slow step, so two loads only take 45 + 45 = 90 minutes. Plenty of time.
You can put both loads in the washer at once, so the whole job is just 75 minutes.

fix_choices.label: Wash load two while load one is in the dryer. You'd be done in two hours.
Buy a second dryer so both loads can dry at the same time.
Skip the dryer and hang both loads. They won't be dry in two hours, but you can still leave.

flaws.explanation: The washer doesn't have to sit and watch the dryer. Wash the second load while the first one dries — two hours on the dot.
flaws.why_tempting: 75 plus 75 is clean arithmetic. It's easy to line the two loads up end to end and forget the machines can work at the same time.
flaws.catch_rule: When two machines can run at once, start the next wash while the first load dries — don't add the full cycles together.
flaws.hint: When the first load moves into the dryer, what's the washer doing?

practice.problem: A printer takes 4 minutes a document, and the binder next to it takes 6. A friend says two documents will take 20 minutes because 10 × 2 = 20. What's wrong?
practice.answer: The second document can print while the first one is being bound: 4 + 6 + 6 = 16 minutes, not 20.

clean_segments: I have to leave in two hours, and I've still got two loads that need to be washed and dried.
The washer takes 30 minutes a load, and the dryer next to it takes 45.
I can wash the second load while the first one dries: 30 plus 45 plus 45 is two hours. I can just make it.
If anyone's nearby later, I may need to borrow a shirt.
clean_conclusion: Wash the second load while the first one dries. That's two hours, just in time.

diagnosis: Two hours means 200 minutes are available.
The deadline is two hours per load.
Only one load needs both washing and drying.
fix: Compare the laundry schedule to 200 minutes.
Give each load its own 120-minute deadline.
Plan to dry only one of the two loads.

diagnosis: The washer takes 45 minutes and the dryer takes 30.
Each quoted time already covers both loads.
The washer and dryer are two names for the same machine here.
fix: Swap the washer and dryer times.
Budget one 30-minute wash for both loads and one 45-minute dry for both.
Schedule all stages as jobs on a single machine.
